audits.title: 860 Intra-Operative Tourniquet Use in Elective Trauma & Orthopaedic Surgery – Do We Accept or Reject Guidelines? (A Multi-Centre Clinical Audit)
audits.standard: BOAST 2021 tourniquet safety: full documentation and pressure based on intra-operative blood pressure
audits.setting: Elective T&O surgery at 3 centres in North London (Royal Free London NHS Trust)

cycle1.result: 14.0% of surgeon notes did not mention tourniquet and 86% incomplete; 97.6% of nursing notes incomplete; upper limb pressure above recommendation in 70% and lower limb above maximal calculated pressure in 47.5%.

audits.other_findings: Mean pressures 237 mmHg (upper limb) and 261.7 mmHg (lower limb); education on guidelines recommended.
audits.citation: Hammond R, Yunus A, Aboutourabi M, Bally D, Igah I, Mann H. 860 Intra-Operative Tourniquet Use in Elective Trauma & Orthopaedic Surgery – Do We Accept or Reject Guidelines? (A Multi-Centre Clinical Audit). British Journal of Surgery. 2023;110(Supplement_7). doi:10.1093/bjs/znad258.675.

audits.title: 964 Intra-Operative Tourniquet Use in Lower Limb Orthopedic Surgery: A BOAST Audit
audits.standard: BOAST: tourniquet pressure systolic plus 70-130 mmHg; ischaemic time less than 120 minutes
audits.setting: Lower limb orthopaedic surgery, single DGH, Mid & South Essex NHS Trust

cycle1.result: Tourniquet use recorded 95.4% (62/66); total time 78.5% (51/66); inflation pressure 58.7% (37/62); 5 (7.6%) exceeded maximum time; mean time 82.4 min, mean pressure 265.7 mmHg.

audits.intervention: Changes to the theatre documentation system; second cycle planned.
audits.citation: Chahal K, Bethel J, Oduoza U, Begum R. 964 Intra-Operative Tourniquet Use in Lower Limb Orthopedic Surgery: A BOAST Audit. British Journal of Surgery. 2024;111(Supplement_6). doi:10.1093/bjs/znae163.282.

audits.title: Improving the Safety of Tourniquet Use in a Trauma Theatre According to the British Orthopaedic Association Guidelines: A Closed Loop Audit.
audits.standard: BOAST guidance on the safe use of intraoperative tourniquets (2021): document skin condition and isolation method, pressure SBP + 50-100 mmHg upper limb and + 70-130 mmHg lower limb in adults, ischaemic time under 120 minutes
audits.setting: Trauma theatre, Trauma and Orthopaedic Department of a district general hospital (Russells Hall Hospital, Dudley)

cycle1.result: Skin status documented 37%; isolation method documented 43%; tourniquet pressure documented 71%; pressure within BOAST safe limit 25%; tourniquet time under 120 minutes in 97%.

audits.intervention: Results presented at departmental audit meeting; tourniquet details made a mandatory part of the electronic operation note template; labels on tourniquet machines to calculate pressure; BOAST guidance posted in the theatre doctors' office.

cycle2.result: Skin status documented 69% (p = 0.004); isolation method 74% (p = 0.003); pressure documented 94% (p = 0.003); pressure within BOAST safe limit 75%; tourniquet time under 120 minutes in 97%.

audits.other_findings: Mean pressure above SBP fell from 125.9 to 99.9 mmHg (upper limb) and 154.2 to 121.7 mmHg (lower limb); about 25% still used pressures above the recommended range and surgeons not using the template still omitted details.
audits.citation: Vayalapra S, Guerero DN, Balasubramanian B, Palaparthy P, Venkatesan M, Sinha M. Improving the Safety of Tourniquet Use in a Trauma Theatre According to the British Orthopaedic Association Guidelines: A Closed Loop Audit. Cureus. 2024;16(1):e51601. doi:10.7759/cureus.51601. PMID: 38313878.

audits.title: Introducing a new proforma for the safe use of intraoperative tourniquets in orthopaedic surgery.
audits.standard: BOAST 'The Safe Use of Intraoperative Tourniquets': document exsanguination method, isolation method, skin condition, pressure and duration; pressure lower limb SBP + 70–130 mmHg, upper limb SBP + 50–100 mmHg; duration ideally < 120 min
audits.setting: Ashford and St Peter's Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust; trauma and elective orthopaedic surgery across both sites

cycle1.result: Exsanguination method documented 5.6%, isolation (shut-off drape) 2.4%, skin condition 0%; duration not in operative note 23.0%, not recorded at all 1.6%; > 120 min in 1.6%; pressure within standard in 24.3% lower limb, 34.8% upper limb and 66.7% paediatric cases.

audits.intervention: Local presentation at trust Quality & Safety Half Day and 'PRESSURE' mnemonic posters in theatres and offices, followed by a new electronic patient record with a tourniquet section and BOAST-based auto-text proforma in the operation note.

cycle2.result: Exsanguination method documented 42.9% (p = 0.001), isolation 42.9% (p = 0.0001), skin condition 64.3% (p = 0.0001); duration not in operative note 10.2% (p = 0.0269), not recorded 0%; none > 120 min; pressure within standard 13.0% lower limb, 35.7% upper limb, 14.2% paediatric (no significant change).

audits.other_findings: An interim re-audit in March 2022 after education alone (n = 153) showed little change (e.g. exsanguination 9.8%, skin condition 5.2%). Staff survey (n = 19) found over 50% sized tourniquets on 'whatever looks the best fit' and 31.6% did not know paediatric pressures.
audits.citation: Garner M, Gaurav G, Shahid Z, Shaunak S, Vats A, Imam M, et al.. Introducing a new proforma for the safe use of intraoperative tourniquets in orthopaedic surgery. Ann R Coll Surg Engl. 2025;107(3):211-216. doi:10.1308/rcsann.2023.0072. PMID: 38578023.

audits.title: Embracing Digital Transformation: A Three-Cycle Audit on Improving Intraoperative Tourniquet Documentation Following BOAST (British Orthopaedic Association Standards for Trauma) Guidelines.
audits.standard: BOAST safe use of intraoperative tourniquets: documented skin checks, isolation, exsanguination, pressure (SBP-based) and time; ischaemic time under 120 minutes
audits.setting: Regional orthopaedic unit, emergency trauma cases, Wythenshawe Hospital, Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: Full adherence 3 (6.0%), partial 16 (32.0%), overall compliance 38.0%; not adhered 31 (62.0%).

audits.intervention: After EPR introduction: survey, department emails and theatre posters; then findings presented at audit meeting and an EPR smart phrase template with drop-downs and automatic SBP calculation introduced.

cycle2.result: Full adherence 9 (18.0%), partial 22 (44.0%), overall compliance 62.0% (p=0.0005 vs 17.0% in cycle 2). Pressure documented 76%, time 94%, skin pre 56%, post 60%, isolation 60%, exsanguination 24%; pressure within standard 24 (63.1%).

audits.other_findings: An intermediate cycle after EPR roll-out (June to July 2023, n=59) fell to 17.0% compliance with 0% skin and isolation documentation. Only 44% of 50 surgeons surveyed knew the BOAST guidance; mean lower limb pressure fell from 287.06 to 265.91 mmHg (p=0.007).
audits.citation: Kafagi AH, Tahoun M, Pillai A. Embracing Digital Transformation: A Three-Cycle Audit on Improving Intraoperative Tourniquet Documentation Following BOAST (British Orthopaedic Association Standards for Trauma) Guidelines. Cureus. 2024;16(7):e65652. doi:10.7759/cureus.65652. PMID: 39205710.

audits.title: Closing the loop on tourniquet safety in distal radius fracture fixation surgery: a two-cycle quality improvement project.
audits.standard: BOAST 'The Safe Use of Intraoperative Tourniquets' (2021): documentation of seven parameters (time, skin condition, padding, site, compressive exsanguination, pressure, size)
audits.setting: Major trauma centre (two hospital sites), University Hospitals Birmingham; distal radius fracture ORIF

cycle1.result: Tourniquet pressure 20.5% (7/34), time 55.9% (19/34); site, padding, exsanguination, skin condition and size all 0%.

audits.intervention: Teaching session for junior doctors and theatre staff, a three-part tourniquet safety checklist in theatres, and BOAST posters in theatre preparation areas.

cycle2.result: Pressure 59.0% (37/63), site 32.0% (20), padding 14.0% (9), exsanguination 13.0% (8), skin condition 11.0% (7), size 10.0% (6), time 56.0% (35).

audits.other_findings: Tourniquet time did not improve and most parameters stayed below 50%. Checklist uptake was not captured; mandatory electronic operative note fields are planned.
audits.citation: Mersal M, Sarofeen S, Embaby O, Shammout S, O'Sullivan C, Lawrence C, et al.. Closing the loop on tourniquet safety in distal radius fracture fixation surgery: a two-cycle quality improvement project. BMJ Open Qual. 2026;15(2):e003956. doi:10.1136/bmjoq-2025-003956. PMID: 42082282.

audits.title: 104 Audit on Adherence to the BOAST Guidelines on the Safe Use of Intraoperative Tourniquets
audits.standard: BOAST guidelines on the safe use of intraoperative tourniquets
audits.setting: Stockport Hospital, elective and emergency procedures

cycle1.result: Pressure recorded in 230 (87.8%) limb procedures; tourniquet type documented in 8.2% and exsanguination method in 34.7%; no record of skin isolation or skin condition.

audits.other_findings: Mean tourniquet time 61.5 minutes, exceeding 120 minutes in 13 cases; re-audit planned in 3-4 months after education and visual aids.
audits.citation: Dosani S, Devarakonda S. 104 Audit on Adherence to the BOAST Guidelines on the Safe Use of Intraoperative Tourniquets. British Journal of Surgery. 2023;110(Supplement_7). doi:10.1093/bjs/znad258.648.

audits.title: 212 An Audit on Single-Centre Compliance with BOAST Standards and Local Infection Control Policy for Safe Intraoperative Tourniquet Use in Plastic Surgery Theatres
audits.standard: BOAST tourniquet standards and trust six-use-day tourniquet infection control policy
audits.setting: Plastic surgery theatres, Mid Yorkshire Teaching NHS Trust (Pinderfields Hospital)

cycle1.result: Operation notes documented duration in 90.3%, type in 67.7%, pressure in 39.5%; skin integrity, isolation and exsanguination not recorded in any notes; fixed 250 mmHg used in 95.3%, exceeding BOAST standards in 53.5%; all within 120-minute limit.

audits.intervention: Teaching session and poster reminders introduced; re-audit planned.
audits.other_findings: Electronic peri-operative pathway had 100% compliance, paper pathways 88.7–97.7%; tourniquets were not marked per trust policy but were disposed of after each list.
audits.citation: Win N, Jivan S. 212 An Audit on Single-Centre Compliance with BOAST Standards and Local Infection Control Policy for Safe Intraoperative Tourniquet Use in Plastic Surgery Theatres. British Journal of Surgery. 2025;112(Supplement_10). doi:10.1093/bjs/znaf128.221.

audits.title: 499 Improving Patient Safety in Upper Limb Surgery: A Closed-Loop Audit of Tourniquet Use Practices Against BSSH/BOAST Guidance in a Tertiary Plastic Surgery Trauma Centre
audits.standard: BOAST/BSSH (2021) guidance on safe use and documentation of intraoperative upper limb tourniquets
audits.setting: Upper limb trauma, tertiary plastic surgery trauma centre (Sheffield Teaching Hospitals)

cycle1.result: Pre-operative skin condition documented 33%, post-operative assessment 0%, skin isolation method 80%, safe tourniquet pressure 94%.

audits.intervention: Departmental teaching, circulation of guideline material, laminated reminders on tourniquet machines and an electronic documentation template.

cycle2.result: Pre-operative skin condition 50%, post-operative assessment 50%, skin isolation method 100%, safe tourniquet pressure 100%.

audits.other_findings: Tourniquet time recording unchanged with 4% lacking clear documentation; no tourniquet burns in either cycle.
audits.citation: Varghesee T, Thomas E. 499 Improving Patient Safety in Upper Limb Surgery: A Closed-Loop Audit of Tourniquet Use Practices Against BSSH/BOAST Guidance in a Tertiary Plastic Surgery Trauma Centre. British Journal of Surgery. 2026;113(Supplement_6). doi:10.1093/bjs/znag063.224.
